With a total area of 42.7 km2 (16.5 sq mi),[[1]](#cite_note-Delhi_Info-1) the municipality of New Delhi forms a small part of the Delhi metropolitan area.[[37]](#cite_note-38) Since the city is located on the [Indo-Gangetic Plain](/wiki/Indo-Gangetic_Plain "Indo-Gangetic Plain"), there is little difference in elevation across the city. While New Delhi lies on the floodplains of the [Yamuna River](/wiki/Yamuna_River "Yamuna River"), it is essentially a landlocked city. Slyly

* One of the team's two mascot's, "Carp Boy"(カープ坊や Kāpu Bōya), is seen in the team's logo. Their other mascot, "[Slyly](/w/index.php?title=Slyly&action=edit&redlink=1 "Slyly (page does not exist)")"(スラィリー Surairī), bears a resemblance to the [Phillie Phanatic](/wiki/Phillie_Phanatic "Phillie Phanatic") of the [Philadelphia Phillies](/wiki/Philadelphia_Phillies "Philadelphia Phillies") and has been with the team since 1995. Both Slyly and the [Phillie Phanatic](/wiki/Phillie_Phanatic "Phillie Phanatic") were designed by [Harrison/Erickson](/wiki/Bonnie_Erickson#Harrison/Erickson,_Inc. "Bonnie Erickson") which has also worked with [Sesame Street](/wiki/Sesame_Street "Sesame Street") and [Jim Henson](/wiki/Jim_Henson "Jim Henson"). The Slyly costume design was also previously used as Duncan the Dragon for the [New Jersey Nets](/wiki/Brooklyn_Nets "Brooklyn Nets").[[11]](#cite_note-11)
* The first Japanese baseball dog "Mickey"(ミッキー Mikkī) was employed between 2005 and 2007. Mickey was a [Golden Retriever](/wiki/Golden_Retriever "Golden Retriever") who wore jersey number 111, and brought new balls to the umpire from the dugout during the game. Mickey died in 2009 at the age of 11.[[12]](#cite_note-12)
* Until 2015, Hiroshima Municipal Stadium was closed every year on August 6 in memorial of the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. The team always played in other stadiums, even if a home game was scheduled for that day. The team played their first August 6 home game at Mazda Zoom Zoom Stadium in 2015. During the game all Carp players wore the uniform number 86 representing the date of the event 70 years prior, and PEACE on the front to symbolize the city's everlasting goal for world peace.[[13]](#cite_note-13)

Considered a significant turning point in the history of the [Hollywood](/wiki/Hollywood_(film_industry) "Hollywood (film industry)") [blockbuster](/wiki/Blockbuster_(entertainment) "Blockbuster (entertainment)"), *Independence Day* was at the forefront of the large-scale [disaster film](/wiki/Disaster_film "Disaster film") and sci-fi resurgence of the mid-late 1990s. It was released worldwide on July 3, 1996, by [20th Century Fox](/wiki/20th_Century_Fox "20th Century Fox"), but began showing on July 2 (the same day the film's story begins) in original release as a result of a high level of anticipation among moviegoers. The film received mixed to positive reviews, with praise for the performances, musical score and visual effects, but criticism for its characters. It grossed over $817.4 million worldwide,[[2]](#cite_note-BOM-2) becoming the [highest-grossing film of 1996](/wiki/1996_in_film "1996 in film") and the [second-highest-grossing film ever at the time](/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films "List of highest-grossing films"), behind *[Jurassic Park](/wiki/Jurassic_Park_(film) "Jurassic Park (film)")* (1993). The film won the [Academy Award for Best Visual Effects](/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Visual_Effects "Academy Award for Best Visual Effects") and was nominated for the [Academy Award for Best Sound](/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Sound_Mixing "Academy Award for Best Sound Mixing").[[4]](#cite_note-OscarNight-4)

The sequel, *[Independence Day: Resurgence](/wiki/Independence_Day:_Resurgence "Independence Day: Resurgence")*, was released 20 years later on June 24, 2016, as part of [a planned series of films](/wiki/Independence_Day_(franchise) "Independence Day (franchise)").

A 2022 study from the [Seoul National University Hospital](/wiki/Seoul_National_University_Hospital "Seoul National University Hospital"),
over more than 4.5 million of people, who were screened over 7 years,
found that[[45]](#cite_note-seoul_2022-45)

* those who increased alcohol consumption had a higher cancer risk (including, but not limited to, alcohol-related cancers) than those who kept the same level of alcohol intake;
* non-drinkers who became mild drinkers had a risk increase estimated at between 0 and 6 percent (meaning slightly greater risk, not 6 percent risk), while non-drinkers who became "moderate" drinkers had a risk increase estimated between 2 and 18 percent.[[46]](#cite_note-46)

The study also had some limitations. For example, the participants were all registered at the South Korean [National Health Insurance Service](/wiki/Healthcare_in_South_Korea "Healthcare in South Korea"), but the study did not take into account alcohol metabolism diseases which are commonly found in East Asia.[[45]](#cite_note-seoul_2022-45)
The participants were not younger than 40.[[45]](#cite_note-seoul_2022-45)
No data was available to account for positive lifestyle and behaviors held during the screening, that may have influenced the cancer risk, nor for the participants' drinking habits that preceded the screening.[[45]](#cite_note-seoul_2022-45)

A prior study found that, "Increasing but moderate alcohol consumption in women was determined to be associated with an increased risk of cancers of the oral cavity and pharynx, esophagus, larynx, rectum, breast, and liver…".[[47]](#cite_note-pmid19244173-47)

Heng joined the Singapore Administrative Service in 1997 and worked at the [Ministry of Education](/wiki/Ministry_of_Education_(Singapore) "Ministry of Education (Singapore)") (MOE) before being appointed [Principal Private Secretary](/wiki/Private_secretary "Private secretary") to [Senior Minister](/wiki/Senior_Minister_of_Singapore "Senior Minister of Singapore") [Lee Kuan Yew](/wiki/Lee_Kuan_Yew "Lee Kuan Yew") that same year. In 2001, Heng was appointed [Permanent Secretary](/wiki/Permanent_secretary "Permanent secretary") at the [Ministry of Trade and Industry](/wiki/Ministry_of_Trade_and_Industry_(Singapore) "Ministry of Trade and Industry (Singapore)") (MTI).[[8]](#cite_note-10)

From 1 June 2005 to 2 April 2011, he served as managing director of the [Monetary Authority of Singapore](/wiki/Monetary_Authority_of_Singapore "Monetary Authority of Singapore") (MAS),[[9]](#cite_note-11) and was named Asia-Pacific Central Bank Governor of the Year by *[The Banker](/wiki/The_Banker "The Banker")* in February 2011.[[10]](#cite_note-12)
